correctness.rationale: PASS: CRT yields phi_P(n)=n product_{p|n}(1-rho_P(p)/p) for arbitrary integer polynomial. For m=ell^a the reduction Phi_m(X) mod ell=(X-1)^phi(m) has one distinct root, whereas for p!=ell the cyclic group F_p^* has phi(m) primitive mth roots exactly if m|(p-1), else none. The global equality cancels the ell factors and becomes product_{other p}(p-rho_m(p))=product_{other p}(p-1). Since phi(m) is even, for odd p!=ell all left factors are odd; parity eliminates any extra odd p when ell=2 and when ell odd with 2 absent. When ell odd and 2 divides n, v2 forces exactly one other odd prime q, where 2(q-rho(q))=q-1; rho=0 impossible, rho=phi(m) implies q=2phi(m)-1 and m|q-1=2(phi(m)-1), contradicting m odd and 0<phi(m)-1<m. Thus no extra prime; conversely ell powers obey both local factors. Independently compared definition and predicted equality for nine indices 3,4,5,7,8,9,11,16,25 and every n=2..300 (2691 pairs). The finite cases are corroboration, not the proof.

The global parity/2-adic obstruction gives a nontrivial all-n theorem beyond the known local root-count formula and can serve as a precise boundary for further non-prime-power indices.

final_claim: For every prime-power cyclotomic index m=ell^a>=3 and integer n>=2, Robu generalized totient counting r mod n with gcd(Phi_m(r),n)=1 equals Euler phi(n) if and only if n=ell^b (b>=1). The local root count rho_m(p) is 1 for p=ell, phi(m) for p!=ell congruent 1 mod m, and zero otherwise.
limitations: Only prime-power cyclotomic indices m>=3 and integers n>=2; neither composite m nor proportionality constants are characterized.
